reuseReview.repository: Reused the existing tools/sp01-taro-probe minimal app and locked React 18.3.1 / TypeScript 5.9.3 versions in an ignored .local candidate.
reuseReview.officialPlatform: Taro v4 supports compiler vite; the official @tarojs/vite-runner 4.3.1 package was inspected from the npm registry tarball.

frameworkPeerDependenciesRelevantToVite.webpack: ^5 (optional peer; not installed in this candidate)

thirdParty.maintainedReleaseEvidence: The official Taro 4.3.1 release page includes Vite runner fixes; npm registry latest tag is 4.3.1, with 4.3.2-beta.2 on the beta tag.

reuseReview.adoptionDecision: Do not adopt: this removes Webpack from the isolated Taro Vite build graph but introduces Vite 4 alongside web Vite 8, leaves the Taro CLI template-download and Swiper dependency paths, and the full candidate audit remains material. Keep the user's confirmed Taro Webpack 5.91.0 exact-peer choice until a complete supported combination resolves R01.

weappBuild.scope: minimal synthetic sample; no product pages

audit.interpretation: npm audit package-entry counts are not product exploitability findings; candidate still has four critical severity entries and requires package-path review

decision.nextAction: Keep the confirmed Webpack 5.91.0 selection. R01 remains pending; when the real mini-program bundle exists, rerun the locked dependency audit and inspect actual product module paths.

limitations: The candidate is an ignored local compatibility probe, not a formal project dependency change.
The Vite build covers a synthetic minimal page, not product screens, runtime behavior, or device acceptance.
Local npm policy skipped eight package install scripts; the strict typecheck and build nevertheless completed successfully in this isolated candidate.
The Vite candidate did not remove the Taro CLI template-fetch dependency or the Taro components Swiper dependency.
The separate web Vite 8.3.5 candidate and mini-program Vite 4.5.14 candidate would create two Vite major versions.
This comparison does not supersede the user's previously confirmed Webpack 5.91.0 choice.
